name: mock-sts-tests
description: Dependencies of the VENDORED protocol jobs in tests/vendored/. Installed separately from the service on purpose — see the comment below and tests/CLAUDE.md.
//: THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE OF .npmrc, AND NOT BECAUSE A SECOND PACKAGE IS
TIDY. The repository root carries `omit=dev` and the Dockerfile passes
`--omit=dev` besides — it is what keeps ldapjs's ~200 test packages out of
the service image — so a devDependency added at the root for the test
suite would be SILENTLY NOT INSTALLED and the jobs needing it would fail
for everybody with a message about a missing binary. The same trap is
already argued for the coverage renderer in tests/CLAUDE.md, which is why
that one is hand-written instead of being c8.
Making them ordinary root dependencies is the other way out and is worse:
selenium-webdriver is a browser driver, and it would then be installed
into the production image of a service that never drives a browser.
So the test dependencies live here, one directory down, where `omit=dev`
does not reach them and the service's own install does not carry them.
`npm install --prefix tests` is the command; tests/Dockerfile runs it
when it builds the tests image that ./run-tests.sh and
./docker-npm-test.sh use, and a job that cannot load because it is
absent FAILS naming this file rather than being skipped.
Everything else those jobs need — bunyan, @xmldom/xmldom, xml-crypto — is
already an ordinary dependency of the service at the repository root, and
node's resolution walks up to find it. Do not duplicate those here: two
copies of one package at two versions is how a test starts disagreeing
with the service about what a signature is.
@noble/* and node-forge are here for the second reason, not the first:
they are what the VENDORED WALLET MODULES need (client/src/pqc.js,
jws.js, jose_jwe.js and the rest), and those are the independent
implementations five jobs verify this service's output against. The two
@noble pins are EXACT and match the parent's, deliberately — a test whose
job is to be a second opinion must not float to a different version of
the curve library than the opinion it is being compared with.
smtp-server (MIT-0) is here for tests/mail.js (#63): an SMTP server
in the test's own process, with STARTTLS, AUTH and a refusal on demand, so
the mail channel's SMTP transport is driven against a real server rather
than a stub. It is the same project as nodemailer, the client it tests.
